title: Observability and Telemetry
description: Add tracing, metrics, and logging to RAG and agent pipelines so you can debug, measure, and improve AI backends.

blocks.text: AI pipelines are harder to debug than traditional APIs because they involve multiple models, retrievers, tools, and conditional branches. Observability must capture the full trace: question, retrieved chunks, tool calls, prompts, model responses, and latency.

blocks.title: Essential telemetry points
items: **User question** — the raw input that started the pipeline.
**Retrieved chunks** — IDs, scores, and metadata for each retrieved passage.
**Tool calls** — name, arguments, result, duration, and errors.
**Prompt tokens** — input token count for cost tracking.
**Completion tokens** — output token count and finish reason.

blocks.text: .NET has first-class OpenTelemetry support. Instrument your RAG and agent pipelines with activities, log scopes, and metrics. Export to Application Insights, Jaeger, or another backend for analysis.

blocks.title: OpenTelemetry RAG pipeline tracing
blocks.content: Instrument a RAG pipeline with activities, metrics, and structured logging.

blocks.title: Trace IDs are your best debug tool
blocks.text: Propagate a single trace ID through ingestion, retrieval, generation, and tool execution. Without it, debugging multi-step agents is extremely difficult.

items.text: I can identify the key events to trace in RAG
items.hint: Question, retrieval, tool calls, prompt tokens, completion, answer

items.text: I know how to instrument .NET with OpenTelemetry
items.hint: Use activities, log scopes, and metrics; export to a backend

items.text: I have a strategy for handling prompt or tool logging safely
items.hint: Avoid logging secrets, PII, or full raw prompts unless explicitly required

blocks.title: Lesson Summary
points: RAG and agents need end-to-end traces, not isolated logs.
Capture retrieval, tool calls, tokens, latency, and final answers.
blocks.takeaway: If you cannot trace the full pipeline, you cannot debug failures or improve quality systematically.
